title: Tiered Notice: Service Artifact Regeneration Plan and Customer Guidance
body:
Executive summary:

This note is a customer-focused status digest and suggested status-page wording for a recent degradation caused by an artifact-regeneration bug in our model cache layer. A subset of requests experienced elevated latency and sporadic 502-style responses between 2029-07-14 02:12 UTC and 2029-07-14 06:45 UTC. The issue affected Hosted API customers with active prefix caching enabled and heavy short-sequence traffic (chat-burst patterns). No data exfiltration or integrity loss has been detected.

Impact (who/how):
- Affected: ~3.2% of total requests across eu-west and us-east regions; concentrated on customers using prefix/KV cache + small prompt sizes (< 64 tokens).
- User visible: increased tail latency (median unaffected, p99 rose from ~420ms to ~1.2s) and intermittent 502 responses during regeneration window. Streaming sessions occasionally dropped and required reconnect.
- Duration: first anomalous event 2029-07-14 02:12 UTC; broad mitigation in place by 2029-07-14 04:10 UTC; full stabilization by 2029-07-14 06:45 UTC.

Root cause (high level):
An internal optimization added in the serving runtime that accelerated on-demand artifact (KV/prefix) recomputation introduced a race when concurrent regeneration and streaming token flushes happened. Under a narrow traffic pattern the artifact state transitioned into a partial/locked state which caused token lookup failures and a small number of requests to surface 502-style errors. The optimization was intended to reduce memory churn but did not account for the streaming-flush interleaving.

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Rolled back the optimization flag at 2029-07-14 04:08 UTC which prevented new regenerations from entering the vulnerable path.
- Activated conservative fallback routing for affected customers (requests routed to a compatible model variant that does prefix-less execution) at 2029-07-14 04:12 UTC to avoid service disruption while preserving availability.
- Applied a hotfix to ensure regeneration uses an exclusive compare-and-swap before the streaming-flush path by 2029-07-14 06:20 UTC.
- Post-fix validation: ramp tests run across eu-west/us-east and production small-sample shadow traffic validated stability; no recurrence in 72 hours.

Customer-facing status-page update (suggested short form):
Title: Brief Service Degradation — intermittent latency and request failures (July 14)
Status: Resolved
Incident window: 2029-07-14 02:12 UTC — 2029-07-14 06:45 UTC
Summary: A subset of requests experienced higher than normal latency and occasional request failures due to an internal artifact-regeneration concurrency bug. We rolled back the vulnerable optimization, applied a targeted hotfix, and routed affected traffic to a compatible fallback. No customer data was exposed.
What we did: Rolled back change, routed traffic to fallback models, deployed hotfix, validated stability.
What you may need to do: If you saw increased error rates or truncated streaming sessions, please retry calls; transient 502s will not impact stored data. Contact support if you see ongoing errors after 2029-07-15.

Customer-facing postmortem (detailed):
1) Timeline (UTC):
   - 2029-07-14 02:12 — First anomaly alert (elevated p99 latency) triggered by synthetic checks.
   - 2029-07-14 02:21 — Increased error rates observed tied to KV/prefix cache operations; SREs paged.
   - 2029-07-14 03:05 — Initial mitigation: throttling of on-demand regeneration attempted; limited success.
   - 2029-07-14 04:08 — Rollback of recent optimization flag initiated.
   - 2029-07-14 04:12 — Traffic routing fallback enabled for affected customer subset.
   - 2029-07-14 06:20 — Hotfix with exclusive CAS guard deployed to runtime.
   - 2029-07-14 06:45 — Normal metrics restored across regions; monitoring switched to enhanced sampling.

2) Technical root cause (more detail):
   - The optimization deferred artifact recomputation to a background worker and signaled readiness with a non-atomic state flag. If a streaming flush concurrently attempted to reference the artifact while the worker had partially built the structure, token resolution could fail and return an internal error path.
   - This manifested only under: high short-sequence throughput + enabled prefix/KV caching + concurrent streaming sessions. The combination is uncommon but present in specific chat/hybrid workloads.

3) Customer impact verification and data integrity: 
   - We examined request logs for impacted customers and verified failed requests correspond to transient internal lookup errors.
   - No requests were silently dropped from user-visible logs beyond the 502s reported; persisted artifacts and customer data were not modified.

4) Permanent remediation and timeline: 
   - Short term (complete): Remove the non-atomic readiness signal and ship the CAS-based hotfix (done 2029-07-14).
   - Medium term (2–4 weeks): Add an integration test harness that simulates concurrent regeneration + streaming flush across model variants. Expected completion: 2029-08-01.
   - Medium term (4–8 weeks): Improve sampling in production to detect this composite pattern earlier and add an automatic degraded-routing rule when prefix regeneration rates exceed threshold. Expected completion: 2029-08-15.
   - Long term (3–6 months): Rework regeneration path to support lock-free incremental patching with formal verification tools to prevent similar races.

5) How we’ll help affected customers:
   - Proactive outreach: CS will email customers who had >0.1% error rate impact in the window with tailored guidance and offer 1:1 post-incident reviews.
   - Credits: We will evaluate usage during the incident window and offer service credits for customers with sustained impact; CS will coordinate on a case-by-case basis.
   - Configuration guidance: For customers with chat-heavy short-sequence traffic, we will share recommended configs (prefetch thresholds and conservative regeneration windows) to avoid exposure until the medium-term changes are in place.

6) Recommended template for your status page entry (concise):
   - Status: Resolved
   - Summary: Intermittent latency and failures caused by artifact-regeneration race; immediate rollback and hotfix applied.
   - Actions for customers: Retry transient errors; contact support if you continue to see issues.

FAQ / anticipated customer questions:
Q: Was customer data compromised?
A: No evidence of data exfiltration or corruption. All persistent artifacts remained intact.

Q: Will this happen again?
A: We shipped a hotfix and have a remediation plan that includes tests and detection. We believe recurrence risk is low, but are treating it as a high-priority reliability investment.

Q: Do I need to change my implementation?
A: No immediate changes required. Customers running extreme chat-burst patterns may adopt the recommended temporary config; we'll provide a checklist and can help via support.

Contact + next steps:
- Primary CS lead: Maya Chen (maya@redwood.ai) — for credits/outreach coordination.
- SRE triage lead: Diego Alvarez (diego@redwood.ai) — for technical follow-ups and 1:1 post-incident calls.
- If you want a tailored writeup for your engineering team or a runbook to avoid similar exposure, reply to this thread or open a support ticket with INC-4521 in the subject.

Notes to internal teams (short):
- Product/Runtime: prioritize integration harness and the sampling instrumentation workstreams.
- Observability: add a dedicated dashboard for regeneration concurrency patterns and an alert that directly triggers degraded-routing.
- Solutions/SEs: prepare customer playbook and small-template rollback instructions for tenants with heavy chat bursts.

End of draft.

(Prepared for publication by CS triage; please review wording for legal or compliance flags before posting to status.redwood.ai.)
